title: A first-in-class, first-in-human study to investigate the safety and tolerability of genetically optimized regulatory T cells (TregTacRes) as add-on therapy for living donor kidney transplant patients.
official: A single ascending dose, first-in-class, first-in-human study to investigate the safety and tolerability of gene-edited regulatory T cells (TregTacRes) as an adjunctive therapy in living-donor kidney recipients - TregTacRes
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the safety, tolerability and feasibility of a single intravenous administration of the gene-edited autologous Treg investigational medicinal product (IMP) TregTacRes in adult recipients of living-donor kidney transplantation receiving standard tacrolimus-based maintenance immunosuppression.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged 18–65 years undergoing a first living-donor kidney transplantation
2. Written informed consent
3. Absence of pre-existing donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies (DSA)
4. Low immunological risk (Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) <20%)
5. Eligibility for protocol-defined maintenance immunosuppressive therapy
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous kidney transplantation or previous transplantation of any other solid organ
2. Any additional immunological finding which, in the opinion of the Principal Investigator, substantially increases the anticipated risk of acute rejection or compromises scientific interpretation of the study
3. Active autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy.
4. Autoimmune disease associated with clinically relevant immune dysregulation that may interfere with assessment of TregTacRes safety, persistence or biological activity
5. Primary or acquired immunodeficiency not attributable to end-stage renal disease
6. Any immune-mediated disorder considered by the Investigator to represent an unacceptable additional risk or compromise interpretation of immune monitoring results
7. Active malignant disease
8. A history of invasive malignancy within the protocol-defined period prior to enrolment unless successfully treated with curative intent and associated with negligible risk of recurrence
9. Any malignant disease considered by the Investigator to increase study-related risk
10. Active bacterial, viral or fungal infection requiring systemic anti-infective therapy
11. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection
12. Planned deceased-donor kidney transplantation
13. Active hepatitis B virus infection
14. Active hepatitis C virus infection
15. Active tuberculosis
16. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) seronegative recipient receiving a kidney from an EBV-seropositive living donor (EBV mismatch).
17. Any clinically relevant opportunistic infection or uncontrolled chronic infection considered by the Investigator to represent an unacceptable risk during study participation
18. Clinically significant cardiovascular disease associated with unacceptable perioperative or study-related risk
19. Clinically significant pulmonary disease like severe irreversible obstructive or restrictive pulmonary disease associated with an unacceptable perioperative or study-related risk
20. Clinically significant hepatic dysfunction and/or decompensated liver cirrhosis
21. Clinically significant haematological or biochemical abnormalities outside protocol-defined eligibility limits
22. Any uncontrolled systemic disease like AL amyloidosis with clinically significant extrarenal organ involvement that, in the opinion of the Investigator, may compromise subject safety or interpretation of study outcomes
23. Combined or multi-organ transplantation
24. Progressive central neurodegenerative disease that may compromise subject safety, informed participation, protocol adherence or interpretation of study outcomes
25. Have previously received any gene therapy or genetically modified cellular therapy
26. Participate in another interventional clinical trial within the protocol-defined wash-out period
27. Ongoing treatment with systemic immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory medicinal products at study entry, except for protocol-permitted low-dose corticosteroid treatment
28. Have a known contraindication or hypersensitivity to any protocol-required medicinal product
29. Concurrent participation in another interventional clinical trial, or previous participation in an interventional clinical trial involving an investigational medicinal product within a period of five elimination half-lives of that medicinal product before planned enrolment, or within any longer period required on the basis of its pharmacodynamic or biological effects
30. Are pregnant or breastfeeding.
31. Have a positive pregnancy test during screening or immediately before transplantation
32. Are women of childbearing potential unwilling to use highly effective contraception throughout the protocol-defined period
33. Are male subjects unwilling to comply with protocol-defined reproductive precautions
34. Any anticipated transplantation procedure considered incompatible with protocol-defined study procedures or assessment of study endpoints
35. Are unable or unwilling to comply with protocol-defined study procedures or long-term follow-up
36. Have a history of alcohol or substance abuse likely to interfere with study participation
37. Are legally incapacitated or otherwise unable to provide valid informed consent
38. Are institutionalised or otherwise considered particularly vulnerable according to applicable ethical guidance
39. Are dependent on the Investigator, Sponsor or study personnel in a manner that could compromise voluntary participation
40. Psychological, psychiatric, familial, social or geographical circumstances that may substantially impair the subject’s ability to comply with study procedures, treatment requirements or the scheduled active and long-term follow-up programme
41. A relationship of dependency on the Sponsor, Investigator, study site or study personnel that could compromise the voluntary nature of informed consent or otherwise render participation ethically inappropriate
42. Subjects shall be excluded if, in the opinion of the Investigator, any medical, psychological or social circumstance exists that: a) places the subject at unacceptable additional risk, b) compromises protocol compliance, c) interferes with interpretation of study endpoints, d) or otherwise renders participation scientifically or ethically inappropriate
43. Presence of clinically relevant donor-specific anti-HLA antibodies (DSA).
44. Positive complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) crossmatch
45. Positive flow-cytometric crossmatch, where performed
46. Panel Reactive Antibody (PRA) exceeding the protocol-defined eligibility threshold
47. Previous treatment with any desensitisation procedure, including but not limited to plasmapheresis, immunoadsorption, intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-CD20 therapy or other antibody-reduction strategies, in preparation for the planned transplantation considered likely to interfere with interpretation of study endpoints
